----------------------------------------------------------------
EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN
----------------------------------------------------------------

1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY
   Strategy:  Within–cashier event-study / difference-in-differences that exploits the discrete, manager-set clock-in / clock-out times of co-workers.  
   • For each focal cashier we compare her scanning speed in the same shift immediately before and after a (quasi-random) “event” in which a very productive peer becomes present (or exits).  
   • Cashier × shift fixed effects absorb all factors that are constant within the shift (store traffic, manager, day-specific promotions, etc.).  
   • 10-minute time-of-day fixed effects absorb systematic intra-shift demand cycles.  
   → Identification comes from minute-to-minute changes that coincide with the sudden presence (or absence) of a high-productivity peer but not with anything else.

   Why appropriate?  
   • Scheduling is done at the *shift* (½-day) horizon and is orthogonal to the minute-to-minute noise we exploit.  
   • The scanner data give exact timestamps, so we can use a tight (e.g., ±30 minutes) symmetric window around the event, minimizing confounds.  
   • Reflection problem is avoided because the treated cashier’s contemporaneous output cannot influence whether the peer has already clocked in.

2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL
   Treatment variable      : Treat_it = 1 if, in 10-minute interval t, cashier i has at least one *visible* coworker j whose permanent productivity P̄_j is in the top 20 % of the store distribution and who just clocked-in ≤ 10 minutes ago (arrival specification) or is about to clock-out (departure spec.).  
   Control group           : Same cashier i in the same shift but in the 30 minutes *before* the peer arrival (or *after* the peer departure). Non-treated cashiers during the same intervals serve as an additional control.  
   Treatment timing        : Discrete events at the peer’s clock-in and clock-out times. We estimate  
                 y_it = Σ_k β_k·LeadLag_k_it + FE_i×shift + FE_time-of-day + ε_it,  
     where LeadLag_k_it captures 10-min leads/lags (k = –3,…,+3).

3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS
   A1. Exogeneity of peer arrival conditional on shift.  
       – Plausible: managers set schedules days ahead; within-shift minute-level variation is not manipulated.  
   A2. No simultaneous demand shock exactly coinciding with the peer’s arrival after conditioning on cashier×shift and time-of-day FE.  
       – Plausible but must be checked by controlling for register-level customer count.  
   A3. No anticipation or learning spillovers within the 30-min window.  
       – Plausible because cashiers do not observe next clock-in times; can be checked by testing for effects in Leads (k ≤ –1).  
   A4. Stable composition of customers and tasks within the window (SUTVA).  
       – Reasonable at 10-minute granularity; customer queues randomly assigned to open lanes.

4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & REMEDIES
   T1. Demand spike (more customers) could trigger both higher cashier speed and additional staff clock-ins.  
        Remedy: Control flexibly for lane-level item count, customer count, and include 10-min store-wide demand FE.  
   T2. Managers may call in *specifically* fast workers at times when overall staffing quality must rise (sorting).  
        Remedy: Shift FE already remove planned staffing differences; restrict to *scheduled* clock-ins only (exclude call-ins/overtime).  
   T3. Mechanical measurement correlation: a “fast” peer increases *average* speed mechanically if we aggregate.  
        Remedy: Unit of observation is *individual* speed, so peer speed does not enter the dependent variable. Use leave-one-out estimator of permanent productivity to avoid mechanical bias.

5. R CODE OUTLINE
```r
# Libraries
library(data.table)   # fast manipulation
library(fixest)       # high-dim FE estimation

# 1. Load data ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Assume cashier_panel.csv has: cashier_id, store_id, lane_id, datetime,
# items_scanned, seconds_worked, peer_id (all coworkers on shift), visible_dummy
dt <- fread("cashier_panel.csv")

# 2. Variable construction ---------------------------------------------------
# 10-minute interval identifier
dt[, interval := floor(as.numeric(datetime)/600)]

# Productivity (items per second)
dt[, prod := items_scanned / seconds_worked]

# Permanent productivity (leave-one-out mean)
dt[, prod_bar := mean(prod), by = cashier_id]
dt[, prod_lo := (sum(prod) - prod)/.N, by = cashier_id]   # leave-one-out

# Flag high-productivity peers in top 20 %
cutoff <- quantile(unique(dt[, .(cashier_id, prod_bar)])$prod_bar, 0.8)
dt[, peer_high := as.integer(prod_bar >= cutoff)]

# For each focal-interval, create indicator: visible high peer just arrived
setkey(dt, store_id, interval)  # for rolling look-ups
# Identify arrivals
dt[, peer_arrival :=
      any(peer_high == 1 & visible_dummy == 1 &
          abs(start_minute - interval*10) <= 10),
   by = .(store_id, interval, cashier_id)]

# Leads and lags (–3,…,+3 => 30 mins)
for(k in -3:3){
  dt[, paste0("L",k) := shift(peer_arrival, n = k, type = "lead"),
                     by = cashier_id]  # lead( ) for k>0, lag for k<0
}

# 3. Main regression (event-study) ------------------------------------------
leadlag <- paste(paste0("L", -3:3), collapse=" + ")
fe_formula <- " + factor(cashier_id_shift) + factor(time10)"
form <- as.formula(paste("prod ~", leadlag, fe_formula))
est <- feols(form, data = dt, cluster = "cashier_id")
summary(est)

# 4. Robustness: placebo with low-productivity coworkers --------------------
dt[, peer_low := any(prod_bar <= quantile(prod_bar,0.2) &
                     visible_dummy==1 &
                     abs(start_minute-interval*10)<=10),
   by = .(store_id, interval, cashier_id)]
form2 <- prod ~ peer_low + factor(cashier_id_shift) + factor(time10)
placebo <- feols(form2, data = dt, cluster = "cashier_id")
summary(placebo)
```

6. EXPECTED RESULTS
Economic intuition: Workers speed up when a more productive peer is watching (social pressure or learning). Prior: scanning speed rises by ~1–3 % (≈0.003–0.01 items/sec on a base of 0.32 items/sec) within 10 minutes after a top-20 % peer arrives; symmetric decrease when the peer leaves. Effect should be stronger when the peer is in direct line-of-sight.

7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST (0 = questionable, 1 = satisfied)
   • Random timing conditional on shift ............... 0.8  
   • No pre-trends (lead coefficients ≈ 0) ............ 1  
   • Correct functional form / FE specification ....... 0.8  
   • No interference outside treated cashier .......... 0.6  
   • Robustness & placebo tests converge .............. 0.8  
   Overall: 4.0 / 5

----------------------------------------------------------------
